PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.

People: Ancient Near Eastern households, herders and farmers.
Dress: Simple wool or linen wraps, tunics and sandals.
Buildings and objects: Wild land, tents, wells, altars and mud-brick towns as the text allows.
Technology: Hand tools, herding, farming and weighed metal; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: (none with fixed canon; show only figures the scene plan describes, or none)

UNSEEN PRESENCE (binding): the light, cloud, smoke, fire and wind in the scene plan are light and weather spread through the place, not one glowing shape. Nobody stands, sits or hovers in them.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Brilliant light and radiant cloud breaking open over the dark waters, with no figure or shape within it.
Action: Light spreads outward from beyond the frame, pushing back the darkness as it first touches the misty surface of the deep.
Setting: Wild, formless primordial waters under a dark void, with mist hanging low and the first dry ground just emerging at the edges.
Secondary elements: Dark churning water surface catching the first glow, mist lifting in pale bands, the faint outline of distant shore or dry ground; no people, creatures, or objects.
Mood: Awe and solemn hush, a sense of beginning and grandeur without spectacle.
Time of day: Primordial darkness giving way to first light; still, misty air with a heavy hush.
Composition: Wide, low viewpoint over the water, with the light entering from the upper or far side and the dark deep filling the lower frame.

Lighting: Strong directional light carved out of shadow; luminous highlights emerging from a mid-tone ground.

Composition: Bold, cinematic massing with one clear focal figure or event; tone carried out to all four edges and corners.

- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, described by the scene plan below.

Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.

Secondary elements: Robed assembly figures in white linen and court robes standing in rows at the edges, rolling fire and drifting smoke through the sky, brilliant white light falling down through the whole vision
Mood: Awe, reverence and solemn expectancy
Time of day: Night vision, lit by a rising radiance that never shifts into day, still air over high cloud

5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.

- Naomi's house in Bethlehem: a modest village dwelling of mud-brick walls and a flat roof of packed earth and beams, with a low doorway and a courtyard of beaten earth. Stone terraces and olive trees stand on the hillside, with grain fields in the valley below and the walls of Bethlehem nearby.
- Only Naomi's house in Bethlehem has this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

Setting: Interior courtyard of a mud-brick house in Bethlehem, with a doorway open to sunlight and a simple stone or clay bench
Secondary elements: Blank, rolled or closed scroll resting on a low table; a few unnamed household members seated nearby, quietly attentive

Lighting: Soft, even daylight or a warm glow; simple shadows and no harsh contrast.
Materials and texture: Flat opaque color with light paper grain and pencil texture inside the shapes.
Composition: Simple, readable staging with one clear focus; generous shapes and background that fill the picture to every edge and corner.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, 1 Samuel 17:49: "David put his hand in his bag, took a stone and slung it, and struck the Philistine in his forehead. The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the earth."

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Kingdoms, exile and return
People: Israelites and neighboring Levantine, Mesopotamian and Persian peoples.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, court robes, priestly linen and period armor.
Buildings and objects: Villages, palaces, temples, city gates and exile settlements.
Technology: Iron and bronze tools, chariots, siege works and scrolls; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: David son of Jesse (king of Israel); Goliath; Philistines

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- David: a beardless youth and young adult before kingship; slender, wiry build, ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes and short dark curly hair. Plain undyed brown wool tunic, leather belt and sandals; shepherd's pouch and sling when called for. No crown or royal robes.
- Goliath: man of enormous height, over nine feet tall, broad-shouldered and heavily muscled, around forty years old. Olive-brown skin, close-cropped dark hair and a full dark beard, strong heavy brow, grave and hard features. Wears bronze scale armour over a linen tunic, bronze greaves, and a bronze helmet, colours of bronze, dark leather and undyed linen. Carries a great spear with a heavy iron head and a sword at his side.
- Valley of Elah: a broad, shallow valley of the Judean lowlands between rounded hills of terraced limestone, with a dry watercourse winding through its floor. Scattered terebinth and oak trees and low scrub grow along the slopes, and sun-baked earth shows pale between rocks. Rough stone walls and simple dwellings of field stone mark the hill ridges.
- Philistines: adult men of the coastal cities, age twenty to forty; medium-to-broad build, sun-browned skin; close-cropped dark hair and a short beard; calm, hard-set features, not caricatured. Typical dress: a knee-length woven tunic of undyed wool with a bordered hem in blue or red, a leather belt and a short cloak of dark wool. Signature props: a bronze helmet with a crest and a round shield, carried by the army; no props carried by the figure alone.
- Gath: a fortified Philistine city on a low hill of the Shephelah, reached by a dusty road from the lowland fields. Thick mudbrick and stone city walls crowned with timber towers, a broad gate of heavy timber and bronze fittings, and tall stone-and-mudbrick houses with flat roofs clustered inside. Olive groves, terraced vineyards and grain fields spread beyond the walls; sycamore and terebinth stand along the road. Cult stands and a temple precinct rise above the houses.

Secondary elements: Bronze-helmeted Philistine soldiers frozen in shock at the front of their ranks; Israelite soldiers on the opposite slope; dust rising from the fallen giant; a shepherd's leather bag at David's side.
Mood: Tense, astonished stillness that gives way to quiet awe and a hint of grief.
Time of day: Late morning, bright and clear, with dry still air stirred only by dust.
Composition: Wide valley view from a low angle, David small in the foreground-center facing the falling Goliath, armies arrayed on both hillsides.

Materials and texture: Flat opaque color with light paper grain and pencil texture inside the shapes.

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- the younger son: Young man in his late teens or early twenties, slender and wiry, with a lean build. Olive skin browned by travel and weather. Dark hair cut short and unkempt, with a short, sparse beard. Face young and open, with weary eyes and a tired mouth. Signature outfit: a sun-faded undyed linen tunic with a dust-brown woollen cloak. Signature prop: a small leather purse at his belt.
- The prodigal's father: man in his late fifties to sixties, of middle height and sturdy, weathered build from years of farm labour; olive skin, lined with sun; close-cropped grey-streaked dark hair and a short greying beard; deep-set, kind eyes and a broad, steady face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic of ochre-brown under a dark russet woollen cloak, with a fringed tzitzit at the hem. Signature props: none carried alone; a bronze signet ring on his hand.
- Galilee: Northern hill country falling to a freshwater lake, the sea of Galilee, its shore lined with fishing boats and nets drying on stone. Low limestone villages of flat-roofed houses, a white stone synagogue with a shallow portico, terraced olive groves, fig trees and scrubland. Roman roads and a distant Gentile town on the slopes.
- Only the younger son, The prodigal's father, Galilee have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

Lighting: Strong directional light carved out of shadow; luminous highlights emerging from a mid-tone ground.
Materials and texture: Granular charcoal texture, smudged and blended passages and crisp accents within the depicted scene; the toned ground is worked over everywhere and reads only as a value inside the picture.

- Goliath: man of enormous height, over nine feet tall, broad-shouldered and heavily muscled, around forty years old. Olive-brown skin, close-cropped dark hair and a full dark beard, strong heavy brow, grave and hard features. Wears bronze scale armour over a linen tunic, bronze greaves, and a bronze helmet, colours of bronze, dark leather and undyed linen. Carries a great spear with a heavy iron head and a sword at his side.
- Valley of Elah: a broad, shallow valley of the Judean lowlands between rounded hills of terraced limestone, with a dry watercourse winding through its floor. Scattered terebinth and oak trees and low scrub grow along the slopes, and sun-baked earth shows pale between rocks. Rough stone walls and simple dwellings of field stone mark the hill ridges.
- Philistines: adult men of the coastal cities, age twenty to forty; medium-to-broad build, sun-browned skin; close-cropped dark hair and a short beard; calm, hard-set features, not caricatured. Typical dress: a knee-length woven tunic of undyed wool with a bordered hem in blue or red, a leather belt and a short cloak of dark wool. Signature props: a bronze helmet with a crest and a round shield, carried by the army; no props carried by the figure alone.
- Gath: a fortified Philistine city on a low hill of the Shephelah, reached by a dusty road from the lowland fields. Thick mudbrick and stone city walls crowned with timber towers, a broad gate of heavy timber and bronze fittings, and tall stone-and-mudbrick houses with flat roofs clustered inside. Olive groves, terraced vineyards and grain fields spread beyond the walls; sycamore and terebinth stand along the road. Cult stands and a temple precinct rise above the houses.

prompt:
PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, Psalms 23:2: "He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters."

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Kingdoms, exile and return
People: Israelites and neighboring Levantine, Mesopotamian and Persian peoples.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, court robes, priestly linen and period armor.
Buildings and objects: Villages, palaces, temples, city gates and exile settlements.
Technology: Iron and bronze tools, chariots, siege works and scrolls; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: (none with fixed canon; show only figures the scene plan describes, or none)

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: A flock of sheep resting on lush green grass beside still water
Action: The sheep lie down contentedly in the grass as the day cools
Setting: Open green pastures and a calm pool of still water in the hill country of ancient Judah
Secondary elements: A shepherd's stone enclosure and distant village walls on the rise, with a staff and sling left propped on a rock nearby
Mood: Peaceful, restful and trusting
Time of day: Late afternoon into evening, clear and calm with soft drifting clouds
Composition: Wide landscape view with the sheep in the foreground lying in grass, the still water at midground and the hills stretching behind

ART STYLE: Soft Pastel
Rendering: A finished soft-pastel painting of the work's world: strokes of chalk pastel layered and blended into glowing color, broken color in the lights and softened edges on distant forms.
Negatives: The pastel covers the whole image: no bare paper margin, vignette into paper tone, border, tape mark or frame, and no signature, initials or caption. Avoid photorealism, hard graphic outlines and cartoon simplification.
Palette: Luminous pastel color: peach and rose light, lavender shadows, warm ochres, sea greens and dusky blues, layered over a mid-tone ground.
Lighting: Gentle, enveloping light, often at dawn or dusk; shadows carry color rather than black.
Materials and texture: Velvety pastel bloom, visible chalk strokes and blended passages within the scene; the toned ground shows only through the strokes, never as bare paper.
Composition: Atmospheric, balanced staging with a clear focal subject; color carried fully to all four edges and corners.

NARRATIVE CONTINUITY (cues only; compose the current moment):
- Before: A Psalm by David. Yahweh is my shepherd; I shall lack nothing.
- After: He restores my soul. He guides me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

effects.planSystem: - Cast marked hasForm: false have no body and are never drawn. When the moment shows one of them appearing or acting, select it and show the moment through the place and the people who witness it. In the scene fields, describe in your own plain words only the physical effects the text names, such as smoke, cloud, fire, storm, wind or light filling a place, spread through the scene or coming from beyond the frame rather than gathered into one glowing shape. Never name it or call it seated, standing, enthroned or riding, and leave out its throne, seat, chariot, robe, train or hem and any face, hands, hair or body: bodily words in the text are metaphors. Say only where those effects are. Whenever the scene keeps light, cloud or fire that comes from it, select it. Keep the people and the place as the subject of the image. A command, oath or mention alone is not an appearance, so add no effect for it then.

effects.reviewFault: a hasForm false entry is given a body, face, hands, clothing, a robe or train, a silhouette, a throne or seat of its own, or is described as seated or standing.

checkFigure.direct: true if any face, head, hands, robe, body or human-shaped silhouette appears inside, made of or emerging from light, radiance, cloud, smoke, fire, a pillar or the sky, or seated or standing on a throne, unless it is clearly one of the beings the description names. Look closely at every bright area, cloud and throne; a faint, translucent or partial figure counts. People standing in the scene, and winged angels or creatures the description names, do not count.
checkFigure.describe: true if a head, face, hands, shoulders or a robed or human-shaped body appears inside, made of or emerging from light, radiance, cloud, smoke, fire, a pillar or the sky, or seated or standing on a throne, unless it is clearly one of the beings the description names. A faint or translucent figure counts if you can point to its head, face, hands or body outline. A flame, a heart-shaped glow or billowing cloud is not a figure. People standing in the scene, and winged angels or creatures the description names, do not count.
checkFigure.brightAreas: What is inside each bright area, cloud, fire, pillar or throne, or "none".
